name: Anger Issues & Irritation
description: Recurrent patterns of anger outbursts, persistent irritability, or difficulty managing frustration that feels out of proportion to situations, affecting relationships and daily functioning.

immediateActions.title: 90-Second Timeout Protocol
instructions: As soon as you feel irritation rising, say silently: I need 90 seconds
If in a conversation, say gently: I need a moment, I will come back in 2 minutes
Physically remove yourself to a quiet space if possible
Splash cold water on your face or hold a cold object
Breathe in for 4 counts, hold 4, exhale 6 — repeat 5 times
Ask yourself: What am I really feeling underneath? Hurt? Fear? Disrespected? Tired?
Wait until you can name the secondary feeling before returning

immediateActions.title: Heat Mapping: Body Scan for Anger
instructions: Close your eyes and mentally scan your body from head to toe
Notice where the anger lives: tight jaw? Clenched fists? Tight chest? Hot face?
Rate the heat/intensity from 1 to 10 in each body area
For the hottest area, breathe INTO it for 3 breaths: imagine cool air flowing in, tension melting out
Clench and release each tight muscle group on each exhale
After releasing, re-rate the intensity and notice the difference

immediateActions.title: Perspective Shift: 3 Angles
instructions: Write the triggering event in 1 sentence
Angle 1 — My view: Write your perspective, your feelings, your assumptions
Angle 2 — Their view: Write what might the other person (or situation) be experiencing? Be generous in imagining
Angle 3 — Observer view: What would a neutral, wise friend say about this?
After writing all 3, ask: Is my original interpretation the only possible one?
Choose one response that would move things forward productively

safetyGuidance: Anger issues are treatable — they often stem from unmet needs, past experiences, or current stressors, and do not make you a bad person. If anger is causing harm to yourself or your relationships, working with a therapist (especially one trained in CBT or DBT) can help you build lasting regulation skills. If you ever feel at risk of harming yourself or someone else, please reach out to emergency services or a crisis line immediately. There is help and you deserve to find peace.
